citation: William Sidney Mount, The Raffle (Raffling for the Goose), 1837, oil on mahogany. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, 97.36, Gift of John D. Crimmins, 1897.
author: William Sidney Mount
repository: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, The American Wing; object 11627 in the museum's collection API (isPublicDomain: true), image at images.metmuseum.org.
locator: The open-access image DT1511 (3811 x 2812): the young man in his shirtsleeves at the centre right, leaning over the table.
rights_note: The Met's Open Access images of public-domain works are released CC0. Used only as a reference picture the 1835 labourer is judged against and for his shirt, waistcoat, neckerchief and hat (T-3450); nothing is traced or sampled from it.
access_notes: Viewed 2026-11-07 (T-3450). Long Island men round a raffle table, 1837. The young man at the centre right wears no coat: a full white shirt with full sleeves gathered at the wrist, a buff waistcoat open at the chest, a red neckerchief knotted loosely at the throat and a pale felt hat with a low crown and a broad soft brim. Rural New York, two years after the scene, not Chicago.
note: One of the 1835 labourer reference set's pictures (data/people_match/reference_sets/labourer_1835.json).
what_it_supplies: a working man in his shirtsleeves and waistcoat, two years after the scene
a knotted neckerchief and a broad-brimmed soft felt hat worn with them
what_it_does_not_supply: the man's trade, or his legs and feet (the table hides them)
anything about Chicago or Patrick Mahoney
